eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 4, Lesson 21
subtitle: The .str accessor — string operations applied to a whole column at once.

caption: Stray spaces, inconsistent capitals, one missing name — exactly what a web form hands you.
strip() trims edges; lower/upper/title fix case. Chain them — each returns a Series with .str again.

eyebrow: Collapsing double spaces with a regex replace
caption: \s+ means one or more whitespace. Always pass regex=True/False explicitly — the default changed between pandas versions.

code:
raw["domain"] = raw["email"].str.split("@").str[1]
raw["domain"].value_counts()
# example.com  3 / shop.io  1 / example.org  1
caption: str.split then .str[1] picks one piece; str[:3] slices the first three characters directly.
na=False treats missing text as "no match" — without it, a missing row breaks the filter.
Each set of parentheses becomes a column. \d digit, \s whitespace, + one or more, . any character.

code:
raw["digits"] = raw["phone"].str.replace(r"\D", "", regex=True)
raw["area"] = raw["digits"].str[:3]
raw["digits"].str.len().tolist()   # [10, 10, 10, 10, 10]
caption: Strip everything that's not a digit, then check the length — 9 or 11 would be a red flag worth investigating.
